methodology: First-pass individual-verse thematic screening; Qur'an passage and cited source translations inspected. No original-language critical edition collation or manuscript verification. No source absence claim. All candidates staged, no public promotions. Open PRs require reconciliation.

records.topic: Covenant binding prophets to recognize and support a later confirming messenger
Submission of heaven and earth to God and return to God
Confession of belief in revelations to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, tribes, Moses, Jesus and prophets
Acceptability of religion and final judgment
Rejection after belief and witnessing the messenger
Judgment and curse on deliberate rejection
Increasing unbelief after belief and rejected repentance

staged_candidates.similarity: Both concern obligations to heed a divinely authorized prophetic messenger.
staged_candidates.difference: Deuteronomy addresses a prophet like Moses arising from among Israel, whereas 3:81 presents a covenant involving prophets and support for a confirming messenger.
staged_candidates.required_check: Hebrew critical edition, textual witnesses, covenant interpretation and history of reception.

staged_candidates.relationship: apostasy and repentance; comparison with significant contrast
staged_candidates.similarity: Both discuss rejection after prior belief/enlightenment and the seriousness of repentance.
staged_candidates.difference: Hebrews 6:4–6 warns against restoring apostates to repentance; Qur'an 3:89 expressly exempts those who repent and reform, while 3:90 addresses continued/increased unbelief. These are not equivalent rules.
staged_candidates.required_check: Greek critical text, rhetorical context, manuscript witnesses, Christian interpretive diversity; do not flatten 3:89 versus 3:90.
